_comment: StructLab material library. EDIT OR EXTEND this file (or load your own copy).
Values are TYPICAL handbook values for learning -- NOT design-certified. Always check
the governing specification / supplier data before real design work.
Typical sources: MatWeb.com typical properties; Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design
(Tables A-5, A-20, A-24); Beer & Johnston Mechanics of Materials (App. B); AISC Steel
Construction Manual; USDA Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-190); ACI 318 (concrete E = 4700*sqrt(f'c) MPa).
Units in this file: E,G in GPa; strengths in MPa; density kg/m^3; cte in 1e-6 per K.
fatigue_strength_MPa is the (completely reversed) strength at fatigue_cycles; if
has_endurance_limit is true it is a true endurance limit (steels), otherwise it is just the
strength at that many cycles (aluminium, titanium, etc.).
yield_MPa for brittle materials is set to the tensile ultimate (no true yield).

materials.name: Gray Cast Iron (Class 30)
materials.notes: Brittle: no true yield. Tensile ultimate used as 'yield'. E varies 66-138 GPa.

materials.name: Copper (C11000)
materials.notes: Annealed values. Cold-worked copper is much stronger.

materials.name: Douglas Fir (along grain)
materials.warning: Wood is orthotropic. Values are ALONG THE GRAIN only; moisture and defects matter.
materials.source: USDA Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-190 (12% MC, approx.)

materials.name: Oak (Red, along grain)
materials.warning: Wood is orthotropic. Values are ALONG THE GRAIN only; moisture and defects matter.
materials.source: USDA Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-190 (12% MC, approx.)

materials.name: Carbon Fiber Composite (UD, fibre direction)
materials.warning: Treated as LINEAR ISOTROPIC. Real composites are strongly anisotropic: properties are for the fibre direction only; transverse and shear strength are far lower.

materials.name: Concrete (f'c = 30 MPa)
materials.warning: Concrete is treated as compression-only: tensile strength is ignored (set to zero). Reinforcement is not modelled.
materials.source: ACI 318: E = 4700*sqrt(f'c) MPa; G from nu = 0.2
